title: 2QBF, blame by a third solver
description: The 2QBF example with a refinement solver. The check returns any y-assignment that falsifies the formula and has no relevant/1 rules; a third solver R receives the candidate and the counterexample over two links and chooses a smallest set of x-variables to blame. Compare the clause lengths with 2QBF and with 2QBF, smallest refinement, where one solver does both jobs.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The formula, as facts. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
term(T) :- xlit(T,_,_).
term(T) :- ylit(T,_,_).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): assignments to the x-variables.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: any assignment to the x-variables (x(I) means that x_I is true).
{ x(I) } :- xvar(I).
#show x/1.
% 'always' is true in every candidate. The check blames it when a counterexample does
% not depend on the candidate: then no candidate is a solution, and the clause "always
% must change" ends the search.
{ always }.
:- not always.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms from A: the x-variables.
fragments.text:
% The check has to know the value of every x-variable.
glue(x(I)) :- xvar(I).
glue(always).

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a y-assignment that falsifies the formula (solver C); no relevant/1 rules.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: an assignment to the y-variables under which every term is false.
1 { yval(J,0); yval(J,1) } 1 :- yvar(J).
% The y-assignment closes a term when it makes one of its y-literals false.
closed(T) :- ylit(T,J,S), yval(J,1-S).
% A term that stays open must be false because of the candidate: bad(T,I) says that
% the literal on x_I in term T is false.
bad(T,I) :- xlit(T,I,1), not x(I).
bad(T,I) :- xlit(T,I,0), x(I).
falsified(T) :- closed(T).
falsified(T) :- bad(T,_).
:- term(T), not falsified(T).
#show yval/2.
% No relevant/1 rules here: solver R works out what to blame.

fragments.name: rglue
fragments.description: The interface atoms from C to R: the y-assignment.
fragments.text:
% The interface atoms of link GC: the y-assignment found by solver C.
glue(yval(J,B)) :- yvar(J), B = 0..1.

fragments.name: blame
fragments.description: Solver R: chooses a smallest set of x-variables to blame and derives relevant/1.
fragments.text:
% Solver R sees the candidate (x/1, through link GA) and the counterexample (yval/2,
% through link GC) and decides which x-variables to blame.
closed(T) :- ylit(T,J,S), yval(J,1-S).
bad(T,I) :- xlit(T,I,1), not x(I).
bad(T,I) :- xlit(T,I,0), x(I).
% One false x-literal per open term keeps that term false ...
1 { blame(T,I) : bad(T,I) } 1 :- term(T), not closed(T).
relevant(x(I)) :- blame(_,I).
% ... and the fewer x-variables are blamed, the shorter the clause.
#minimize { 1,I : relevant(x(I)) }.
% If the y-assignment closes every term on its own, no candidate is a solution at all:
% blame the atom that is always true.
open :- term(T), not closed(T).
relevant(always) :- not open.

fragments.name: blame_all
fragments.description: Variant blame-all: solver R blames every false x-literal of the open terms (no choice, no #minimize).
fragments.text:
% Solver R sees the candidate (x/1, through link GA) and the counterexample (yval/2,
% through link GC) and decides which x-variables to blame.
closed(T) :- ylit(T,J,S), yval(J,1-S).
bad(T,I) :- xlit(T,I,1), not x(I).
bad(T,I) :- xlit(T,I,0), x(I).
% Blame every false x-literal of every open term (the refinement of the plain 2QBF example).
relevant(x(I)) :- bad(T,I), not closed(T).
% If the y-assignment closes every term on its own, no candidate is a solution at all:
% blame the atom that is always true.
open :- term(T), not closed(T).
relevant(always) :- not open.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
solver R = shared + blame
link G  = A -> C via shared + glue
link GA = A -> R via shared + glue
link GC = C -> R via shared + rglue

# C finds any y-assignment that falsifies the formula. A third solver R then sees the
# candidate (link GA) and the counterexample (link GC) and chooses a smallest set of
# x-variables to blame; GA.clause reads relevant/1 from R's model.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            Y = R.solve(assume GA(M), GC(X), optimal)
            reject M with GA.clause(M, Y)

instances.facts:
% A quantified Boolean formula  exists x1..x6  forall y1..y5 : T1 v ... v T12,
% where each term T is a conjunction of literals.
% xlit(T,I,S): term T contains x_I (S = 1) or its negation (S = 0); ylit/3 likewise.
xvar(1..6).  yvar(1..5).
xlit(1,2,0). xlit(1,5,1). ylit(1,3,0).      % ~x2 & x5 & ~y3
xlit(2,6,0). ylit(2,2,1). ylit(2,5,1).      % ~x6 & y2 & y5
xlit(3,2,1). xlit(3,5,0). ylit(3,4,1).      % x2 & ~x5 & y4
xlit(4,4,0). ylit(4,1,1). ylit(4,4,0).      % ~x4 & y1 & ~y4
xlit(5,4,1). xlit(5,5,0). ylit(5,3,1).      % x4 & ~x5 & y3
xlit(6,4,1). ylit(6,2,0). ylit(6,3,1).      % x4 & ~y2 & y3
xlit(7,5,0). ylit(7,1,1). ylit(7,5,1).      % ~x5 & y1 & y5
xlit(8,3,0). ylit(8,2,0). ylit(8,4,1).      % ~x3 & ~y2 & y4
xlit(9,1,0). ylit(9,3,0). ylit(9,4,0).      % ~x1 & ~y3 & ~y4
xlit(10,6,0). ylit(10,1,1). ylit(10,3,1).   % ~x6 & y1 & y3
xlit(11,5,1). xlit(11,6,0). ylit(11,2,0).   % x5 & ~x6 & ~y2
xlit(12,6,1). ylit(12,2,1). ylit(12,4,1).   % x6 & y2 & y4

% A false formula: y1 = y2 = 0 makes every term false, whatever the x-variables are.
% exists x1 x2  forall y1 y2 : (x1 & y1) v (x2 & y1) v (~x2 & y2).
xvar(1..2).  yvar(1..2).
xlit(1,1,1). ylit(1,1,1).
xlit(2,2,1). ylit(2,1,1).
xlit(3,2,0). ylit(3,2,1).

% A random formula with 5 x-variables, 4 y-variables and 10 terms (random-3 of qbf).
xvar(1..5).  yvar(1..4).
xlit(1,4,0). ylit(1,1,0).
xlit(2,1,0). ylit(2,1,0).
xlit(3,3,0). ylit(3,1,0).
xlit(4,3,0). ylit(4,1,0).
xlit(5,2,0). ylit(5,1,1).
xlit(6,1,0). ylit(6,1,0).
xlit(7,1,0). ylit(7,1,0).
xlit(8,3,0). ylit(8,1,0).
xlit(9,3,0). ylit(9,1,0).
xlit(10,4,0). xlit(10,5,0). ylit(10,1,0).

% A random formula (generator qbf-dnf, nx = 6, ny = 6, t = 14, seed 3) that is false:
% no x-assignment survives, but it takes several counterexamples to show it.
xvar(1..6).  yvar(1..6).
ylit(1,2,0). ylit(1,4,1). ylit(1,6,0).   % ~y2 & y4 & ~y6
xlit(2,5,0). ylit(2,4,1). ylit(2,5,1).   % ~x5 & y4 & y5
xlit(3,1,0). xlit(3,6,1). ylit(3,4,1).   % ~x1 & x6 & y4
xlit(4,2,1). xlit(4,5,0). ylit(4,2,0).   % x2 & ~x5 & ~y2
ylit(5,1,1). ylit(5,5,0). ylit(5,5,1).   % y1 & ~y5 & y5
xlit(6,3,1). ylit(6,2,1). ylit(6,6,0).   % x3 & y2 & ~y6
xlit(7,1,0). xlit(7,3,0). ylit(7,4,1).   % ~x1 & ~x3 & y4
xlit(8,6,1). ylit(8,1,1). ylit(8,2,1).   % x6 & y1 & y2
xlit(9,1,1). ylit(9,4,1). ylit(9,5,1).   % x1 & y4 & y5
xlit(10,3,1). ylit(10,1,1). ylit(10,3,1). % x3 & y1 & y3
ylit(11,1,1). ylit(11,3,1). ylit(11,4,0). % y1 & y3 & ~y4
xlit(12,1,0). xlit(12,1,1). xlit(12,5,1). % ~x1 & x1 & x5
xlit(13,6,1). ylit(13,4,1). ylit(13,6,1). % x6 & y4 & y6
xlit(14,4,1). ylit(14,3,0). ylit(14,4,0). % x4 & ~y3 & ~y4

generators.name: qbf-dnf
generators.description: A random exists-forall QBF with a DNF matrix: t terms of three literals over nx + ny variables.
generators.text:
% qbf-dnf: exists x1..x_nx forall y1..y_ny : T1 v ... v Tt, three literals per term.
% Each literal picks one of the nx + ny variables uniformly and a sign with probability 1/2.
xvar(1..nx).  yvar(1..ny).
term(1..t).  slot(1..3).
var(T,J,@int(1, nx+ny, T, J)) :- term(T), slot(J).
sign(T,J,@flip(500, T, J, sign)) :- term(T), slot(J).
xlit(T,I,S) :- var(T,J,I), sign(T,J,S), I <= nx.
ylit(T,I-nx,S) :- var(T,J,I), sign(T,J,S), I > nx.

#show xvar/1.  #show yvar/1.  #show xlit/3.  #show ylit/3.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
solver R = shared + blame
link G  = A -> C via shared + glue
link GA = A -> R via shared + glue
link GC = C -> R via shared + rglue

# candidate (link GA) and the counterexample (link GC) and chooses a smallest set of
# x-variables to blame; GA.clause reads relevant/1 from R's model.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            Y = R.solve(assume GA(M), GC(X), optimal)
            reject M with G.block(M)
